commitment.heading: Our commitment
commitment.body: Family HQ is built for every member of every family. We design and develop with accessibility as a baseline — not an afterthought — and we want to hear from you when we get it wrong.

conformance.heading: Conformance target
conformance.body1: We aim to meet {{target}} of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, and to exceed it where we can. This is the legal minimum for public-facing services under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).
conformance.body2: Conformance is verified by a combination of automated checks (axe-core in our continuous-integration pipeline), structured manual review by our team, and ongoing feedback from people who use Family HQ. We treat reported barriers as bugs and triage them with the same urgency.

limitations.heading: Known limitations
limitations.intro: We publish what we know is not yet conformant so you can plan around it and so we are accountable to fixing it:
limitations.atTesting: Real-user assistive-technology testing is scheduled but has not yet been completed against this build. If a screen reader, voice control, or switch device fails for you, we want to know.
limitations.audit: Independent third-party accessibility audit is scheduled before public launch.
limitations.french: French-language translation review by a native-speaker reviewer is scheduled before public launch — the current French copy is a developer-authored placeholder.

feedback.heading: Report a barrier or request an alternative format
feedback.body1: If you encounter an accessibility barrier in Family HQ, or you need information from this site in an alternative format (large print, plain text, an accessible electronic format, or another arrangement that works for you), please contact us:
feedback.body2: We aim to acknowledge every report within two business days and to provide a substantive response within ten business days. Please include the page or flow where the barrier appeared, the assistive technology you were using, and a description of what went wrong.

welcome.title: Welcome to Family HQ
welcome.body: This is your family's shared home base. A quick tour shows you what's where — you can skip it any time and re-open it from your Account.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.body: Plan family events together. Tap a day to see what's on. Parents can add events; everyone in the family can see them.

board.title: Board
board.body: A bulletin board for the family — quick notes, reminders, photos of the school field trip. The newest post sits at the top.

chores.title: Chores
chores.body: Track who's doing what. Members mark their chores complete; parents approve and the allowance ledger updates automatically.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: The newest tab — a shared to-do list and routine checklists for the whole family. Anyone can add a to-do, check items off a morning routine, or start a fresh run. No allowance, no approval — just things that need doing.

allowance.title: Allowance
allowance.body: A read-only ledger of every approved chore and the running balance. Members see their own; parents pick whose to view.

family.title: Invite the family
family.body: From your Account menu, tap "Manage family" to send each member a one-tap invite link. Pending invitations expire after 14 days, and you can rename, deactivate, or revoke any invite at any time. Members don't see this section.

contact.heading: Questions or concerns
contact.body: If you have a question about this document, want to exercise your rights, or want to report a concern, please contact us at the address below. We aim to acknowledge every message within five business days.

scope.heading: What this policy covers
scope.body: This policy describes what personal information Family HQ collects when you create an account, what we do with it, who we share it with, and how you can exercise your rights over it. It applies to use of the Family HQ web application and any related services we operate under the same brand. We are a Canadian service and we treat the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) as our baseline.

data.heading: What we collect
data.body: When you sign up, we collect the email address you use to sign in and, if you choose, a display name and an avatar. Inside the app you create family-scoped content (chores, calendar events, allowance entries, board posts) — that content is stored against your family and visible only to members of your family. We also collect minimal technical information (device type, browser language, an anonymous session identifier) to keep the service running and to investigate problems. We do NOT collect advertising identifiers, build behavioural profiles for targeted advertising, or sell information about you to anyone.

sharing.heading: Who we share data with
sharing.body: We share information only with the service providers we need to operate Family HQ: an authentication and database provider (Google Firebase) that holds your account credentials and your family's content under contractual data-processing terms, and a transactional email provider when we need to send you account-related messages. We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. If we are ever required by law to disclose information, we will narrow the scope of any disclosure to what the law actually requires and, where permitted, notify you.

retention.heading: How long we keep data
retention.body: We keep your account information for as long as the account is active. When you delete a family, the family content (chores, events, posts, allowance entries) is removed from the live database within thirty days. Backups age out on a rolling schedule no longer than ninety days. Authentication records may be retained for a longer period to detect fraud and abuse, but are isolated from the live application and not used for any other purpose.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: You can access, correct, export, or delete your personal information at any time. You can request a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct anything that is inaccurate, ask us to delete your account, or withdraw your consent to our processing. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at the address below and we will respond within thirty days. If you are not satisfied with our response, you have the right to file a complaint with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.

changes.heading: Changes to this policy
changes.body: When we make a material change to this policy, we will update the 'Last reviewed' date above and, for changes that affect how we collect or use your information, post a notice in the application or send a message to the email address on your account. The current version is always available at this address; previous versions are archived on request.

scope.heading: What this agreement covers
scope.body: These terms are the agreement between you and the operators of Family HQ for your use of the Family HQ web application. By creating an account or using the service you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service. We may update these terms over time; the current version is always available at this address.

data.heading: Your account
data.body: You are responsible for the email address and credentials you use to sign in. Choose a strong password and do not share your credentials with anyone outside your household. If you suspect your account has been accessed by someone you did not authorise, contact us promptly. The first person to create a family becomes a parent of that family; parents control membership, content visibility, and allowance balances within their family.

sharing.heading: Acceptable use
sharing.body: Family HQ is a household tool. Do not use it to harass, threaten, or intimidate anyone, to post content that is unlawful or that infringes someone else's rights, to attempt to access another family's content, or to interfere with the service's normal operation. We may suspend or terminate access for violations of this section, and where appropriate, cooperate with law enforcement.

retention.heading: Service availability
retention.body: We try to keep Family HQ running and to make backups, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted service or that no data will ever be lost. Treat any information you store in the service as something you would not be devastated to lose. We will tell you about planned maintenance windows that we expect to be visible, and we will publish incident updates when something unexpected goes wrong.

rights.heading: Liability and warranties
rights.body: The service is provided 'as is' and 'as available.' To the maximum extent permitted by law, we disclaim warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. Our liability for any claim arising from your use of the service is limited to the amount you paid us for the service in the twelve months before the claim arose; for free use of the service, that amount is zero.

changes.heading: Governing law and changes
changes.body: These terms are governed by the laws of Ontario, Canada, and the federal laws of Canada applicable in Ontario. When we make a material change to these terms, we will update the 'Last reviewed' date above and, for changes that materially affect your rights or obligations, post a notice in the application or send a message to the email address on your account.
